descripcion_es: Actions in progress in the past and background actions; when and while.
resumen: The past continuous (was / were + -ing) describes an action that was in progress at a moment in the past. It is like Spanish “estaba + gerundio” or the Spanish imperfect.

items: Action in progress at a specific moment: At eight o'clock I was having dinner.
Background action interrupted by a shorter one (past simple): I was cooking when the phone rang.
Two long actions at the same time: While I was working, my sister was watching TV.
Describing the setting of a story: The sun was shining and people were walking in the park.

explicacion.texto: When usually introduces the short action (past simple); while, the long action (past continuous). When I arrived, they were eating. / While they were eating, I arrived.
State verbs (know, like, want, believe, own) are not normally used in the continuous form: I knew the answer, not I was knowing.
Notice the difference: When she arrived, we had dinner (we had dinner after she arrived) versus When she arrived, we were having dinner (we were already having dinner).

ejemplos.frase: I was walking home when I saw the accident.
ejemplos.traduccion: Iba andando a casa cuando vi el accidente.

ejemplos.frase: What were you doing at ten last night?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Qué estabas haciendo anoche a las diez?

ejemplos.frase: While Ana was studying, her flatmates were making a lot of noise.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mientras Ana estudiaba, sus compañeros de piso hacían mucho ruido.

ejemplos.frase: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
ejemplos.traduccion: Estaba lloviendo, así que nos quedamos dentro.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: When I arrived, they were eat.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: When I arrived, they were eating.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: State verbs do not usually take the continuous form.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: While I was having a shower, the doorbell was ringing.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: While I was having a shower, the doorbell rang.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The short action that interrupts is in the past simple.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the past continuous.
ejercicios.frase: At midnight we ___ (dance) in the square.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the first rule in Rules and key points: an action in progress at a specific moment in the past. The clue is at midnight, an exact time at which the action had already started and had not finished yet. The subject we requires were, and the verb takes -ing: dancing (dance loses the final e).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Action in progress at a specific moment: were + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: A medianoche estábamos bailando en la plaza.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With we you use were, not was.
Verbs ending in a silent e lose it when you add -ing: dancing.
The past simple does not express that the action was in progress at midnight; the instruction asks for the past continuous.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the past continuous.
ejercicios.frase: My father ___ (drive) when he heard the news.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of the background action interrupted by a shorter one in the past simple. The clue is when he heard the news: hearing the news is brief and happens while he is driving. That is why the long action is in the past continuous, with was for the singular subject my father: was driving.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi padre iba conduciendo cuando oyó la noticia.

errores_previstos.explicacion: My father is singular: was.
The past simple does not present the driving as a background action in progress; the instruction asks for the past continuous.
After was the verb takes -ing: driving.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the negative form of the past continuous.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Negative” row of the table: subject + wasn't / weren't + -ing. The clue is the plural subject the students, which requires were, and the instruction to use the negative. Pay attention is a fixed expression and pay takes -ing: paying. Both the contraction and the full form are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los alumnos no estaban prestando atención.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The past continuous is made negative with wasn't / weren't, not with did.
The students is plural: weren't.
After weren't the verb takes -ing: paying.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the past simple or the past continuous.
ejercicios.frase: I was having breakfast when the postman ___ (knock) on the door.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of the interrupted background action: the long action is in the past continuous and the short one in the past simple. The clue is that the long action (was having breakfast) is already written and that when introduces the single event. Knocking on the door is instant, so it is in the past simple: knocked.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The short action that interrupts is in the past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estaba desayunando cuando el cartero llamó a la puerta.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The short action that interrupts is in the past simple; in the continuous it would seem that someone was knocking for a long time.
The past form is missing: knocked.
It is present; the story is in the past: knocked.

ejercicios.frase: I was reading in bed ___ the lights went out.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in Rules and key points: when usually introduces the short action (past simple) and while the long one (past continuous). The clue is that after the gap comes the lights went out, in the past simple and instant. That is why it is when; while does not introduce single, brief actions.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The short action in the past simple is introduced with when; while is not used with single, brief actions.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estaba leyendo en la cama cuando se fue la luz.

errores_previstos.explicacion: While introduces the long action in progress; here what follows is a short action in the past simple, which goes with when.
During is a preposition and is followed by a noun (during the night), not by a clause.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Question” row of the table: Was / Were + subject + -ing. The clue is when I called you: the question asks about the action that was in progress when the call came. With you you use were, and in the question it goes before the subject.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Question about the action in progress: Were + subject + -ing.

por_opcion.did you do: Incorrect in this sense: it would ask what you did in reaction to the call, after it, not what you were doing at that moment.
por_opcion.were you doing: Correct: it asks about the action in progress, with were before the subject.
por_opcion.you were doing: Incorrect: in a direct question the auxiliary goes before the subject; this order is only correct in indirect questions (Tell me what you were doing).

ejercicios.frase: She ___ her ankle while she was running.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of the short action that happens during a long one: the short one is in the past simple. The clue is while she was running, the long action already in the continuous. Breaking an ankle is instant, so it is in the past simple, with the irregular past of break: broke.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Short action that happens during a long one: past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se rompió el tobillo mientras corría.

por_opcion.broke: Correct: short action in the past simple within the long action.
por_opcion.was breaking: Incorrect: it would present the break as a long process, which makes no sense for something instant.
por_opcion.breaks: Incorrect: it is present and the sentence is in the past.

ejercicios.frase: ___ the film started, everybody stopped talking.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule about when and while: when introduces the single action in the past simple. The clue is the film started, a short action in the past simple, followed by another action also in the past simple: one happens immediately after the other. While would require a long action in progress.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: When introduces a single action in the past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando empezó la película, todo el mundo dejó de hablar.

por_opcion.When: Correct: it introduces a single event in the past simple.
por_opcion.While: Incorrect: while introduces a long action in progress (While the film was playing…), not an instant beginning.
por_opcion.During: Incorrect: during is a preposition and is followed by a noun (during the film), not by a clause with a verb.

ejercicios.frase: I ___ that you were in Madrid.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule about state verbs: know, like, want, believe or own are not normally used in the continuous form. The clue is know, which expresses a mental state, not an action in progress. That is why it is in the negative past simple: didn't + infinitive (know). Spanish uses the imperfect here, which pushes learners towards the mistake of the continuous form.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Know is a state verb: it does not take the continuous form.
ejercicios.traduccion: No sabía que estabas en Madrid.

por_opcion.wasn't knowing: Incorrect: know is a state verb and does not take the continuous form.
por_opcion.didn't know: Correct: negative past simple of a state verb.
por_opcion.weren't knowing: Incorrect: besides the state verb mistake, with I you would use wasn't.

ejercicios.enunciado: Turn the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Question” row of the table: Was / Were + subject + -ing. The clue is were in the affirmative sentence, which you simply put before the subject they, without adding did. The rest of the sentence does not change, and it ends with a question mark.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The past continuous does not use did; the question is formed by inverting were and the subject.
Calque of Spanish intonation: in written English the question requires inverting were and the subject.
With they you use were.

ejercicios.frase: We was watching TV when the lights went out.
respuestas: We were watching TV when the lights went out.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table of forms: was with I, he, she, it; were with you, we, they. The clue is the subject we, which requires were. The rest of the sentence is correct: the long action in the continuous and the short one (went out) in the past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estábamos viendo la tele cuando se fue la luz.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We was watching TV when the lights went out.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the uncorrected sentence: with we you use were.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We were watching TV when the lights were going out.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It corrects was but puts the short interrupting action in the continuous; went out must stay in the past simple.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We watched TV when the lights went out.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It loses the meaning of an action in progress; besides, the mistake was in was, not in the tense.

ejercicios.frase: While I was cooking, I was cutting my finger.
respuestas: While I was cooking, I cut my finger.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of the short action that interrupts the long one and the third typical mistake in the card. The clue is while I was cooking, the background action; cutting your finger is instant and must be in the past simple. Cut is irregular and its past form is the same as the infinitive: cut.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Cutting yourself is a short action that interrupts: past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mientras cocinaba, me corté el dedo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: While I was cooking, I was cutting my finger.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the uncorrected sentence: the short action is in the past simple.

errores_previstos.respuesta: While I was cooking, I cutted my finger.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Cut is irregular: the past form is cut.

errores_previstos.respuesta: While I cooked, I was cutting my finger.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It reverses the roles: the long action is cooking (continuous) and the short one is cutting yourself (simple).

respuestas: She was talking on the phone
Was she talking on the phone
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Affirmative” row of the table: subject + was + -ing. The clue is that the words include was and talking, and the fixed expression on the phone. The order is she + was + talking + on the phone. The question, with was before the subject, is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estaba hablando por teléfono. (También: ¿Estaba hablando por teléfono?)

errores_previstos.respuesta: she was talking the on phone
errores_previstos.explicacion: The article goes with the noun: on the phone.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she talking was on the phone
errores_previstos.explicacion: Was goes before the -ing verb.

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Question” row of the table with a question word: why + were + subject + -ing. The clue is why, which opens the question, and were, which must go before the subject you. Laughing ends the question.

errores_previstos.explicacion: That order belongs to an indirect question; in a direct question were goes before you.
The question word goes at the beginning of the question.

descripcion_larga_es: The past continuous (was / were + -ing) describes what was in progress at a moment in the past and serves as the background to the short actions told in the past simple. It is the basis for telling stories, anecdotes and events. Spanish speakers find it hard to distinguish from the past simple because the Spanish imperfect covers uses that English divides between the two tenses, and because state verbs do not allow the continuous form.

contexto.que_es: It is the tense formed with was or were and the verb in -ing. It expresses an action in progress at a specific past moment, a long action interrupted by a short one, two long actions at the same time or the setting of a story. It is similar to Spanish “estaba + gerundio”.
contexto.por_que_importa: Without it you cannot tell a story well in English: it marks what was happening and what happened suddenly. If you confuse it with the past simple, the order of events changes (When she arrived, we had dinner versus we were having dinner). It is a classic point in A2 and B1 exams and in any narrative oral test.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: With specific times or moments in the past (at eight o'clock, at midnight), with while for the long action and combined with when + past simple for the interruption. Also in background descriptions in a story. Spanish speakers tend to use the continuous form for everything that would be in the imperfect in Spanish, including state verbs like know or want, and to put the interruption in the continuous as well.
